svg.title: What one client owns, between a host and a single server
svg.desc: A host box on the left and a server box on the right, the same size as each other, with request and response arrows between them and a note that the messages crossing are tools/call, tools/list, resources/read and prompts/get. Between them a large container labelled client holds five numbered parts: the transport, which may be standard input and output, Streamable HTTP or an in-process server object; request identifier correlation, which matches each response to the caller waiting on it; the capability cache, which holds the list results for the time to live the server put on them; the multi round-trip driver, which answers an input_required result and retries with the echoed request state; and the result reader, drawn taller because it carries the branch the post is about. Inside the result reader, a red box says a raised call and a result carrying isError true both become an outcome whose ok flag is false, and a green box says the success path keeps all five content block types plus the structured content. A band across the bottom states the lifetime rule: the client wraps a task group, a task group must be exited by the task that entered it, and a hand-rolled close method leaks the subprocess it was written to reap.
svg.text: One client per connected server. Four parts on the way out, one on the way back.
the protocol-speaking object. Not the host, not the interface.
Matches each response to the caller waiting on it.
The list results, held for the ttlMs the server put on them.
Answers input_required, then retries with requestState.
The return path, and the one branch everybody forgets.
The lifetime rule: the client wraps a task group, and a task group must be exited by the task that entered it.
Use async with, or an AsyncExitStack in one task. A hand-rolled close() leaks the subprocess it was written to reap.
